criteria.thresholds: 2+ of 11 criteria over 12 months; Mild: 2-3, Moderate: 4-5, Severe: 6+ (DSM p.553-555)

epidemiology.prevalence: 29.1% US adults lifetime, 4.6% adolescents 12-17 (DSM p.552-553; Dulcan p.225)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Peak 18-25 years; median first drink age 13, regular use age 14 (DSM p.553; Dulcan p.225)
comorbidities: Conduct Disorder / ODD 4x increased risk (Dulcan p.225-226)
epidemiology.prognosis: Variable; drinking onset <21 increases adult dependence risk 7x (Dulcan p.226-227)

etiology.genetic: 40%-60% heritability; ALDH2/ADH flush reaction protective, Low Level of Response (LR) increases risk (DSM p.557-558)
etiology.neurobiology: Mesolimbic DA (VTA -> NAc) shift to Dorsal Striatum (habit circuit); GABA_A PAM, NMDA/mGluR/VSCC inhibition, mu-opioid endorphin release (StahlNeuro p.539-555)
etiology.environmental: Top-down PFC vs Bottom-up limbic maturation imbalance in adolescents, peer influence, family SUD (Dulcan p.217, 226)

first_line: Acamprosate - mGluR/GABA modulator, safe in liver disease (StahlNeuro p.555, 557)
Benzodiazepines for acute withdrawal: Diazepam/Chlordiazepoxide front-loading or symptom-triggered (DSM p.565; Dulcan p.611)
Family-based therapies for adolescents: MDFT, A-CRA, FFT, MST (Dulcan p.235-236)
second_line: Lorazepam / Oxazepam / Temazepam (LOT) for liver impairment/cirrhosis (DSM p.556; Dulcan p.345)
Clonidine - adjunctive for autonomic symptoms (StahlKids p.150)
key_side_effects: Disulfiram: severe flushing, vomiting, hypotension with alcohol (StahlNeuro p.554)
Benzodiazepines: sedation, paradoxical agitation in children/adolescents (Dulcan p.345)
Naltrexone: hepatotoxicity at high doses (StahlNeuro p.555)
treatment.monitoring: CIWA-Ar protocol for withdrawal severity; LFTs, CDT, GGT, BAC, urine toxicology for relapse (DSM p.558-559; Dulcan p.611)

items: CRAFFT screening tool for adolescents: Car, Relax, Alone, Forget, Friends, Trouble (Dulcan p.229)

CDT and GGT state markers for heavy drinking and relapse monitoring (DSM p.558-559)

CDT >= 20 U/L indicates heavy drinking (DSM p.559)

items: Delirium Tremens (Alcohol Withdrawal Delirium) is a life-threatening medical emergency (DSM p.565)

Requires ICU admission, IV high-dose BZDs, fluid/electrolyte correction, IV Thiamine (DSM p.565; Dulcan p.348)
key_numbers: 48-72 hours post-cessation typical onset for DT (DSM p.565)

5%-15% mortality rate even with treatment (DSM p.565)

items: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency due to poor nutrition, malabsorption, and impaired enzyme conversion (DSM p.556, 714-715)
Thiamine FIRST before glucose/dextrose infusion to prevent precipitating acute Wernicke Encephalopathy (DSM p.715)
Wernicke Encephalopathy acute triad: Confusion, Ataxia, Ophthalmoplegia/Nystagmus (CN VI) (DSM p.714-715)
Korsakoff Syndrome chronic stage (F10.26): severe anterograde amnesia, retrograde amnesia, confabulation (DSM p.587, 712, 714-715)
key_numbers: 1 absolute rule: Thiamine before glucose infusion (DSM p.715)
3 classic features in Wernicke triad: confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia (DSM p.714-715)
F10.26 ICD-10 code for Korsakoff Syndrome (DSM p.587)

high_yield: AUD diagnosis requires 2+ of 11 DSM-5-TR criteria over 12 months; medical prescription tolerance/withdrawal excluded (DSM p.553-554).
Adolescent AUD first-line treatment is evidence-based family therapy (MDFT, A-CRA); zero FDA-approved drugs for <18 (Dulcan p.234-236).
Sinclair Method: Naltrexone taken 1 hour before drinking induces pharmacological extinction of habit circuit in Dorsal Striatum (StahlNeuro p.571-572).
LOT rule in liver cirrhosis/failure: Lorazepam, Oxazepam, Temazepam undergo glucuronidation only, bypassing CYP450 (DSM p.556; Dulcan p.345).
Withdrawal timeline: 6-12h tremor/autonomic, 12-48h seizures & alcoholic hallucinosis (intact sensorium), 48-72h Delirium Tremens (DSM p.564-565).
Delirium Tremens carries 5%-15% mortality rate; managed in ICU with high-dose IV BZDs (DSM p.565).
CRITICAL: Always give Thiamine (Vitamin B1) BEFORE Glucose infusion to prevent Wernicke Encephalopathy (DSM p.715).
